headline: Hong Kong's government set out a four-step plan to help young people get entry-level work as AI takes over routine first-job tasks.
score_reason: Matches pool score; regional policy plan, official source.
importance_line: It affects Hong Kong graduates and employers, but the plan is a set of announced programmes and its effect on jobs is not yet shown.
summary: The South China Morning Post reports on a speech by Hong Kong's innovation and technology official Kevin Choi, whose text the Hong Kong government published, describing a four-step 'talent ladder' from mass AI training to infrastructure and policy. Choi called the 'entry-level shock' real and cited a two-year 30,000-place youth employment and internship programme and 27 new AI-related degree programmes.
notes: SCMP original blocked; entry built from the government speech text (HKSAR press release carried by Bastille Post) plus SCMP's headline. Source label AI News Desk, outlets named in summary.
